static_traits.name: Lin An
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with peers were strained for a time; has a few close friends in the dance circle to discuss professional challenges, but finds it hard to voice inferiority and feelings of not being good enough
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received psychotherapy before; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly logical; cooperative but slightly tense; can notice and describe their own thought patterns (e.g. 'should be perfect', 'I am utterly useless'), tending toward harsh self-criticism and absolutist statements

basic_info.main_problem: When making mistakes in dance or being unable to perform a piece perfectly, I feel intense inferiority and worthlessness, falling into a cycle of self-criticism.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I want to stop always feeling so defeated when things go wrong.'
growth_experiences: Strong perfectionist tendencies and fear of failure formed from adolescence; once a mistake occurs in dance, it is taken as proof of inadequate ability, gradually affecting self-esteem and mood.

In a recent major dance competition, one misstep disrupted the entire performance; afterward, intense feelings of 'worthlessness' and self-blame grew, self-esteem suffered, and realizing the negative impact on mental health and performance led to seeking counseling.

special_situations.event: In a large dance competition, a mistake in one movement leads to abnormal subsequent performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not one hundred percent perfect, it proves I don't deserve to be a dancer, I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: After a competition, intensifies self-reproach and doubles training, forcing themselves with higher standards to avoid making mistakes again; avoids expressing vulnerability to maintain the 'must be perfect' image
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I shouldn't make mistakes; a real dancer wouldn't be like this; I don't deserve to stand here

special_situations.event: Small mistakes in rehearsal or unsuccessful learning of new moves
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes now, it means I'll never learn in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated practice, longer training time, using self-criticism to 'motivate' oneself to avoid failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I'll never do well; this is a waste of time

special_situations.event: After matches/rehearsals, reviews performance and receives feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only zero mistakes deserve affirmation; no other strengths count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing only on error details, ignoring highlights and effort in the performance; negating positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The parts done well don't matter; what really matters is that I made a mistake

special_situations.event: Thinks of judges', peers', and audiences' views of the performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake, I'll disappoint everyone, proving I shouldn't be here
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding revealing feelings of not being good enough to friends, bearing pressure alone to avoid judgment

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain recognition and a sense of worth through perfect performance
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated, humiliated, or excluded after failure
defense_goal: Controls and avoids failure with strict self-criticism and high standards
Avoiding expressing vulnerability to prevent others from seeing imperfection

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a self that could fail at any moment
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judger / others easily disappointed
Teammates and audience I let down

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When it is mentioned that 'making mistakes is part of learning' or when invited to focus on positive aspects and progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting imperfection as evidence of 'failure', worrying that relaxing standards will be seen by others as unprofessional
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone is restrained and self-reproachful, emphasizing one's own inadequacy and responsibility, downplaying external situational factors, expressing doubt about or negating positive feedback.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Facing high-standard demands during evaluations, competitions, or contact with authorities (judges/coaches)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing external standards unconditionally as the only correct standard, which must be met with perfection
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using absolutist language of 'should/must', emphasizing rules and standards; tone is serious, emotional expression reduced, technical details and norms highlighted.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Being invited to talk about feelings rather than just technical issues during post-competition or rehearsal reviews
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Emotions are seen as factors that interfere with performance; believes rational analysis and error correction are 'safer'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone is calm, focusing on technique and improvement strategies, downplaying subjective feelings of shame and loss, using objective terms instead of emotional vocabulary.

manifestations: Lives alone; emotionally finds it hard to open up to friends about feelings of not being good enough
Harsh self-criticism leads to relationship tension with peers, experiencing relationship estrangement
outcomes: Worsening impaired self-esteem and sense of frustration
Under pressure, more prone to bear it alone and avoid seeking help

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently judging oneself by the internal rule of 'should/must be perfect'
Uncritically treating external high standards as the sole criterion for measuring self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-blame and self-labeling after mistakes ('I am useless')
Difficult to receive positive feedback, overly concerned about possible negative evaluation

positive_force: Has a few trustworthy friends in the dance circle, with some social support
Willing to try new cognitive perspectives and exercises (such as gratitude records, restructuring thoughts)
Able to self-observe and identify negative automatic thought patterns
Has the habit of persistent training and self-reflection, and is action-oriented
negative_force: Perfectionism and strong fear of failure; value is excessively attached to performance outcomes
Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, intensifying self-denial
Negating the positive and mental filtering, struggling to see progress and strengths
Self-labeling and personalized attribution, easily experiences shame and guilt
Struggling to express vulnerability and ask for help, increased sense of relational distance

target_behavior.behavior: Harsh self-criticism and negative self-labeling (e.g. 'I am utterly useless')
antecedent: Making mistakes while dancing or not yet reaching perfect standards
High-pressure demands in competition or evaluation situations
Unsuccessful learning of new moves in rehearsal
target_behavior.core_reason: Perfectionism and fear of failure, tying self-worth to flawless performance, forming 'black-and-white' conditions of worth
target_behavior.function: Avoids failing again and gains a sense of control through self-blame and high-pressure self-control
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-esteem, interpersonal tension, impaired sleep and self-care, affected performance quality and attendance

target_behavior.behavior: Mental filtering and negating the positive (focusing only on mistakes, disparaging progress and strengths)
antecedent: Reviewing performance after the game / rehearsal
When receiving affirming feedback from others
target_behavior.core_reason: The negative core belief 'I am not good enough' maintains attentional bias and selective evidence gathering
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a self-consistent negative schema, avoiding facing vulnerability and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent frustration and anxiety, impaired motivation, decreased error-correction efficiency, worsening the negative emotion cycle
